entries.meaning: To break food up with your teeth before swallowing it. ---
examples: Chew your food slowly — it helps digestion.
The puppy chewed the corner off my shoe.
She sat chewing gum and staring out the window.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (chew your food), intransitive (chew slowly)
entries.phrasal verbs: chew on · chew out · chew over · chew up

entries.meaning: Swallow has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Swallow the pill with plenty of water.
He swallowed the last bite and stood up.
She winced, swallowing the bitter medicine.
I'm not going to swallow that excuse.
They swallowed the whole story without asking a single question.
He had swallowed every word of it.
She swallowed her pride and asked for help.
You learn to swallow your anger in this job.
He has swallowed a lot of insults from that man.

senses.head: To make food or drink go down your throat
examples: Swallow the pill with plenty of water.
He swallowed the last bite and stood up.
She winced, swallowing the bitter medicine.

senses.head: To believe something that is not true
examples: I'm not going to swallow that excuse.
They swallowed the whole story without asking a single question.
He had swallowed every word of it.

senses.head: To hold back a feeling instead of showing it
examples: She swallowed her pride and asked for help.
You learn to swallow your anger in this job.
He has swallowed a lot of insults from that man.

entries.русский: глотать, проглотить; проглотить (ложь), поверить (во что-то сомнительное), купиться; подавлять (чувство), сдерживать; проглотить (обиду)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (swallow a pill), intransitive (it hurts to swallow)

entries.meaning: To eat something noisily and steadily, usually a crunchy snack. ---
examples: The kids munch popcorn through the whole movie.
He munched on carrot sticks while he waited.
I could hear someone munching chips behind me.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (munch popcorn), intransitive (munch on chips)
entries.contrast: Verbs ending in -ch add -es in the third person: he munches.

entries.meaning: Devour has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Teenagers devour whatever is in the fridge.
He devoured two plates of pasta in ten minutes.
The cake had been devoured before I got a slice.
He devours two or three novels a week.
She devoured the whole series in a weekend.
I have devoured everything that author has written.

senses.head: To eat something quickly and hungrily
examples: Teenagers devour whatever is in the fridge.
He devoured two plates of pasta in ten minutes.
The cake had been devoured before I got a slice.

senses.head: To read or watch something eagerly and quickly
examples: He devours two or three novels a week.
She devoured the whole series in a weekend.
I have devoured everything that author has written.

entries.русский: пожирать, жадно съедать; проглатывать (книгу), зачитываться, поглощать

entries.meaning: To eat small amounts of food between meals. ---
examples: I snack too much when I study.
We snacked on almonds during the drive.
She has been snacking all afternoon.
entries.contrast: Takes on before the food: snack on nuts, never 'snack nuts'.

entries.meaning: To eat a large, festive meal with great enjoyment. ---
examples: Every November they feast on turkey and pie.
We feasted until nobody could move.
The guests were feasting while the cook rested.
entries.contrast: Takes on: feast on lobster.

entries.meaning: To eat dinner, especially in a restaurant or in a formal setting. ---
examples: They dine out every Friday.
We dined on the terrace as the sun went down.
We were dining when the power went out.
entries.contrast: The silent -e disappears before -ing: dining with one n.

entries.meaning: Digest has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Babies cannot digest solid food yet.
He never fully digested that fried chicken.
Sit still for a while — your body is digesting lunch.
Give me a minute to digest that.
She digested the report on the flight home.
The team is still digesting the news.

senses.head: To break food down in the stomach so the body can use it
examples: Babies cannot digest solid food yet.
He never fully digested that fried chicken.
Sit still for a while — your body is digesting lunch.

senses.head: To take in new information slowly until you understand it
examples: Give me a minute to digest that.
She digested the report on the flight home.
The team is still digesting the news.

entries.русский: переваривать, переварить; усваивать, усвоить; осмысливать, переваривать (информацию)
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed on the second syllable (dy-JEST); the noun a digest on the first.

entries.meaning: Consume has 4 distinct senses.

He consumed three liters of water that day.
The label shows how many calories you are consuming.

The project consumed most of our budget.
Data centers are consuming more electricity every year.

Flames consumed the warehouse in twenty minutes.
The old barn was consumed by the blaze.
Guilt consumed him for years.
She was consumed by jealousy.
Work seems to consume his whole life.

senses.head: To eat or drink something, especially in a measured amount
examples: Americans consume a lot of sugar.
He consumed three liters of water that day.
The label shows how many calories you are consuming.

senses.head: To use up fuel, money, time, or other resources
examples: The old furnace consumes a lot of gas.
The project consumed most of our budget.
Data centers are consuming more electricity every year.

senses.head: To destroy something completely, said of fire
examples: A fire can consume a dry forest in hours.
Flames consumed the warehouse in twenty minutes.
The old barn was consumed by the blaze.

senses.head: To fill someone's mind so completely that nothing else matters
examples: Guilt consumed him for years.
She was consumed by jealousy.
Work seems to consume his whole life.

entries.русский: потреблять, употреблять в пищу; потреблять, расходовать, израсходовать; пожирать, уничтожать (об огне); поглощать, снедать (о чувстве)

entries.meaning: To eat or drink something with a loud sucking noise. ---
examples: Please don't slurp your soup at the table.
He slurped the last of the noodles.
Someone behind me was slurping iced coffee.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (slurp your soup), intransitive (stop slurping)

entries.meaning: To swallow a drink or food quickly in large mouthfuls. ---
examples: Don't gulp your milk like that.
He gulped the water and asked for more.
She was gulping air after the run.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (gulp your milk), intransitive (he gulped nervously)

entries.meaning: Chug has 2 distinct senses.
examples: College kids chug soda at parties.
He chugged a bottle of water after practice.
They were chugging lemonade in the heat.
Old tractors chug up that hill all summer.
The train chugged out of the station right on time.
A little boat was chugging across the bay.

senses.head: To drink a whole drink quickly without stopping, in informal speech
examples: College kids chug soda at parties.
He chugged a bottle of water after practice.
They were chugging lemonade in the heat.

senses.head: Of a train or an engine, to move along making a heavy, repeated sound
examples: Old tractors chug up that hill all summer.
The train chugged out of the station right on time.
A little boat was chugging across the bay.

entries.русский: пить залпом, осушать одним махом; пыхтеть, тарахтеть (о поезде, моторе)

entries.meaning: To brown bread or nuts with dry heat, or to raise a glass in someone's honor. ---
examples: Toast the bread while I fry the eggs.
We stood and toasted the newlyweds.
She is toasting almonds for the salad.

entries.meaning: To satisfy your thirst with a drink. ---
examples: Nothing quenches thirst like cold water.
The lemonade quenched our thirst in seconds.
He drank soda after soda without quenching anything.
entries.contrast: Almost always with thirst; -ch takes -es: quenches.

entries.meaning: Starve has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I'm starving — when is dinner?
Whole villages starved that winter.
He has starved himself on that diet for weeks.
Budget cuts starve rural clinics of nurses.
The program was starved of funding for years.
You are starving that plant of light.

senses.head: To suffer or die from a lack of food
examples: I'm starving — when is dinner?
Whole villages starved that winter.
He has starved himself on that diet for weeks.

senses.head: To keep a person, a place, or a thing from getting something it badly needs
examples: Budget cuts starve rural clinics of nurses.
The program was starved of funding for years.
You are starving that plant of light.

entries.русский: голодать, умирать с голоду; лишать необходимого, недофинансировать; морить (голодом, без средств)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (starve yourself), intransitive (the cattle starved)
entries.contrast: In everyday speech I'm starving just means 'very hungry'.

entries.meaning: To go without food for a period of time, often for religious or medical reasons. ---
examples: Many people fast during Ramadan.
She fasted for twelve hours before the blood test.
He has been fasting since sunrise.
entries.contrast: Spelled like the adjective fast 'quick', but the meanings are unrelated.

entries.meaning: To limit what you eat in order to lose weight. ---
examples: She diets every January.
He dieted for months before the wedding.
I'm dieting, so no cake for me.
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t is not doubled: dieted, dieting.

entries.meaning: To want a particular food or drink very badly. ---
examples: Pregnant women often crave strange foods.
I craved salt for days after the flu.
He has been craving his mother's soup.

entries.meaning: Choke has 4 distinct senses.
examples: Cut the grapes so the baby doesn't choke.
He choked on a fish bone at dinner.
She started choking and someone slapped her back.
Loosen that collar before it chokes the dog.
The wrestler choked his opponent until the referee stepped in.
The dog had been choking itself pulling against the leash.
Great players don't choke in the last minute.
He choked and missed both free throws.
Our team has choked in the playoffs three years running.
Weeds choke the flower beds every August.
Traffic choked the tunnel for two hours.
The creek was choked with fallen branches.

senses.head: To be unable to breathe because food or drink is blocking your throat
examples: Cut the grapes so the baby doesn't choke.
He choked on a fish bone at dinner.
She started choking and someone slapped her back.

senses.head: To squeeze someone's throat so that they cannot breathe
examples: Loosen that collar before it chokes the dog.
The wrestler choked his opponent until the referee stepped in.
The dog had been choking itself pulling against the leash.

senses.head: To fail at the important moment because of nerves
examples: Great players don't choke in the last minute.
He choked and missed both free throws.
Our team has choked in the playoffs three years running.

senses.head: To fill a space so completely that nothing can move through it
examples: Weeds choke the flower beds every August.
Traffic choked the tunnel for two hours.
The creek was choked with fallen branches.

entries.русский: давиться, подавиться; душить, задушить; сдавать (о нервах), оплошать в решающий момент; забивать, заполнять до отказа; заглушать (о сорняках)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the smoke choked us), intransitive (he choked on a bone)
entries.contrast: Takes on before the food: choke on a bone.
entries.phrasal verbs: choke back · choke down · choke off · choke up

entries.meaning: To bring food up from the stomach and out through the mouth. ---

She vomited twice during the night.
He was pale and vomiting by morning.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (vomit blood), intransitive (he vomited twice)
entries.contrast: First-syllable stress, so the t is not doubled: vomited, vomiting.

entries.meaning: Burp has 2 distinct senses.
examples: It's rude to burp at the table.
The baby burped and fell asleep.
She is burping him after his bottle.
Burp the baby before you put her down.
He burped the twins one after the other.
She was burping the baby when the phone rang.

senses.head: To let air come up noisily from the stomach through the mouth
examples: It's rude to burp at the table.

She is burping him after his bottle.

senses.head: To pat a baby on the back so that it brings up swallowed air
examples: Burp the baby before you put her down.

She was burping the baby when the phone rang.

entries.русский: рыгать, отрыгнуть; помогать срыгнуть (ребёнку), держать столбиком

senses.head: To show someone to a place to sit, especially in a restaurant
examples: The host will seat you in a moment.

senses.head: To have enough seats for a particular number of people
examples: The hall seats about four hundred people.
The original stadium seated only twenty thousand.
Once the patio is finished, the restaurant will seat ninety.

entries.русский: усаживать, сажать за столик; вмещать, быть рассчитанным на (число мест)

senses.head: To get yourself or someone else ready for something that is going to happen

examples: Don't fry the fish too long.

She is frying bacon for the sandwiches.

Too much voltage will fry the chip.

examples: Don't fry the fish too long.

She is frying bacon for the sandwiches.

senses.head: To ruin an electrical device by overheating it or running too much current through it (informal)
examples: A power surge fried the router.

entries.meaning: To heat or cook food in a microwave oven. ---
